payload.text: Add UI setting in the setting window for affective dialog and proactive audio.

**Defining New App Features**

I'm currently updating the `AppConfig` type to accommodate new UI settings. These will control 'affective dialog' and 'proactive audio' for the Gemini Live sessions. Adding these toggles to the settings window is next on my to-do list. I'm focusing on ensuring these additions integrate cleanly with the existing configuration structure.


**Incorporating New Preferences**

I've added the new boolean fields, `enableAffectiveDialog` and `enableProactiveAudio`, to the `AppConfig` interface. I've also set default values for them in `constants.ts`, aligning with the existing behavior. I'm now working on integrating these new settings into the UI, specifically updating `Settings.tsx` to include the respective checkboxes. Finally, I'll update `geminiLive.ts` to consume these config options during API connection setup.


**Adapting Configuration Options**

I'm updating the `geminiLive.ts` service to utilize `config.enableAffectiveDialog` and `config.enableProactiveAudio` instead of hardcoded values. I'll need to refactor the configuration object within the service to reference these new properties from the `AppConfig`. Simultaneously, I'll be adding the corresponding checkboxes to `components/Settings.tsx` to allow user control. These additions are planned for the Vision/Tracking or a new Audio section.


**Integrating Configuration Changes**

I've refactored `geminiLive.ts` to consume the new `enableAffectiveDialog` and `enableProactiveAudio` flags from the `AppConfig`.  I'm focusing on ensuring these preferences correctly control the respective behaviors in the Gemini Live sessions.  I'm also updating the relevant UI components to provide user controls for these new settings, planning to group them in the Vision/Tracking or a new Audio settings section.


**Implementing UI Controls**

I'm now integrating the new checkboxes into `components/Settings.tsx`. This includes adding HTML for each checkbox, along with handlers to update the `config` state. I'm focusing on ensuring that the user's preference for `enableAffectiveDialog` and `enableProactiveAudio` correctly maps to the corresponding boolean values in the application config. I'll make sure to group these settings logically, possibly in a new Audio section.


**Reviewing Configuration Logic**

I'm verifying that the updated `App.tsx` correctly handles the new configuration options. Specifically, the component now merges saved configurations with `DEFAULT_CONFIG` which is in `constants.ts`, ensuring that the new `enableProactiveAudio` and other new properties are always present, either from storage or defaults. I'm focusing on confirming that any missing preferences in saved configurations default to the newly set values in constants.


**Consuming Configured Settings**

I'm now integrating the `enableAffectiveDialog` and `enableProactiveAudio` flags into the `geminiLive.ts` API call. Specifically, I'm updating the call to use the values defined in the `AppConfig` type to ensure the desired behavior is enabled or disabled correctly based on user preferences. I'm focusing on ensuring this change aligns seamlessly with the UI updates.


**Implementing New Data Structures**

I'm currently working on defining new data structures. Specifically, I'm adding `MoveCommand` and `SystemStatus` interfaces to handle robot movement and system health information, respectively. I'll need to define how these will be consumed and displayed in the application, and ensure they are compatible with the existing data flow. I'm also ensuring the types are correctly imported and used throughout the codebase.


**Mapping Animation Commands**

I'm currently working on mapping the user's animation requests, like "Twerk" or "Lie-Sit-Lie", to the robot's actual motion functions. I need to define the corresponding function calls. For example, 'Twerk' needs to use a `moveHip` or similar command, and 'Lie-Sit-Lie' would probably involve `sit()`, `lieDown()`, and then back to `sit()` calls. I will have to test them out!


**Populating Animation Data**

I'm expanding the animation data to include more options for robot movements. I've populated new animation command data, adding descriptions and labels for easier selection. This includes adding new animations like 'Downward Dog', 'Sneeze', 'Spider', 'Swim', 'Wave', and 'Jump', each with descriptions. I'm also including new model options for AI interaction and voice options for the assistant.


**Finalizing UI Integration**

I'm finishing the integration of the new model and voice options into the UI. I've populated the UI with the `MODEL_OPTIONS` and `VOICE_OPTIONS` from `constants.ts`. I'm now working on the functionality to ensure these settings are correctly saved and applied when a user makes a selection.  The selections will update the main configuration object.


**Integrating Config Selections**

I'm now integrating the selections for model and voice from the UI to the `AppConfig`. The UI updates the `config` state on selection. I need to ensure this correctly updates in the application. I will focus on proper state management and validation during the settings updates. This allows the saved configurations to keep pace with UI inputs.


**Validating Configuration Updates**

I'm now validating the updated configuration logic, specifically focusing on the new settings in `App.tsx`. I'm confirming that the merging of saved configurations and defaults in `constants.ts` works as intended, ensuring all new properties are present and correctly prioritized. This involves thorough testing of different user scenarios and saved configurations. I'm also ensuring the correct updates occur.


**Validating User Interface Logic**

I'm now making sure the checkboxes for 'Enable Affective Dialog' and 'Enable Proactive Audio' work correctly with the application's config state. I've placed the HTML for the checkboxes inside the settings UI, and confirmed their boolean values correctly reflect the config state. I am ensuring that the correct values are being rendered and that the UI responds to user input.


**Adjusting Camera Settings**

I'm currently working on adjusting camera settings in the UI. I have added a checkbox to enable/disable video, and a selection dropdown for camera source, either the browser webcam or the robot's local server. I'm also adding a new select to control the eye-tracking source. I'm ensuring these UI elements correctly update the `config` state, which will control app behaviors.


**Integrating Camera Options**

I've integrated new UI elements to control camera settings.  I'm adding a checkbox for video enablement and dropdowns for camera and eye-tracking sources.  I've connected these UI elements to the application state using state variables.  The configuration objects should be updated when the user changes these settings. I must ensure the application behavior correctly reflects these changes.



**Consolidating Settings Integration**

I'm now focusing on integrating the camera options, along with the 'Enable Affective Dialog' and 'Enable Proactive Audio' preferences, to a common settings panel within the UI. I'm ensuring all these settings are correctly reflected in the `AppConfig`.  I'm focusing on UI/UX, ensuring settings are clearly grouped and accessible. I will test all possible configurations.


**Refining Robot Control**

I'm currently working on refactoring existing animation commands and adding a series of robot movement tools. These will control the robot's physical actions like walking and motor control. I need to ensure these controls are available and ready to use, including a description of how they work.


**Implementing Movement Controls**

I'm now implementing the robot's movement controls, allowing direct commands like "Move forward," "Turn left," and so forth. I'm building on the basic motion functions for each component. I will write the basic wrappers for the underlying APIs. I will also be working on the parameter validation, ensuring safe values and ranges.


**Updating Movement Commands**

I'm now refining the robot movement commands, adding options for velocity and duration for complex control.  I'm adding validation to ensure safe parameter ranges.  I'm focusing on defining and documenting these new commands, ensuring they are easy to understand and use. I need to make sure the syntax is correct.


**Implementing Video Processing**

I'm now integrating the script processor node and media stream for video processing. I'm focusing on setting up the audio context and creating the analyser node to capture audio levels. The queued sources array is initialized. All the existing callbacks have been connected and now ready to handle video processing.


**Analyzing Audio Visualization**

I'm now focusing on integrating the audio analysis components for the visualization of speaker sound. I've successfully implemented the audio analyser node and configured its parameters for real-time processing. Next, I'll connect the analyser to the audio context and start monitoring the output volume for visual representation.


**Constructing Audio Analysis**

I'm working on connecting the audio analyser node to the audio context for real-time sound visualization. I have configured the analyser node's parameters and connected it to the audio context for real-time sound analysis. Now, I'm working to display the visual results.


**Initializing Audio Input**

I'm now setting up the audio input. Specifically, I'm configuring the `AudioContext` and creating an analyser node to capture audio levels. I'm also preparing the script processor for real-time analysis. The `startOutputVolumeMonitoring` function is implemented to capture output volume.


**Refining Audio Processing**

I'm focusing on the implementation of the `onaudioprocess` callback for real-time audio input. The setup includes managing the `MediaStreamSource`, `AudioContext`, and `ScriptProcessorNode`. I've connected the source, process the input data, and sending it to a session. Error handling is improved to gracefully handle session closing. Video processing will come soon.


**Implementing Image Capture Logic**

I'm currently working on implementing the image capture logic for both browser webcam and server-based camera sources. I'm focusing on ensuring consistent image encoding and data transmission to the AI session, regardless of the camera source. I'm also addressing the issue of null blobs and session promise handling for robustness.


**Evaluating Image Processing**

I'm now evaluating the newly implemented image capture logic. I'm focusing on ensuring that images from both the browser webcam and the server-based camera are correctly encoded and sent to the AI session. The integration of null blob handling and session promise management is crucial. I must ensure these work.


**Updating Movement Controls**

I'm now implementing the `move_robot` command with new logic and parameters for velocity. I'm focusing on parsing the `args.direction`, `args.speed`, and `args.duration` to create correct velocity vectors. I'm also addressing safety checks and ensuring the robotBridge method is called with these new inputs.


**Implementing Movement Commands**

I'm now implementing the `move_robot` and `turn_robot` tools to control robot movement. For `move_robot`, I'm parsing direction, speed, and duration for velocity vectors. For `turn_robot`, I'm calculating angle and duration based on turn direction. I'm ensuring both commands correctly queue motions with the robot bridge.


**Enhancing Video Handling**

I'm currently working to integrate the browser video element with the existing image capture and processing pipeline. I'm focusing on getting the video stream into a suitable format for the audio analyser. I'm also ensuring the existing processing logic continues to function seamlessly with this new source. I'm making sure to address any performance concerns.


**Enhancing Video Integration**

I'm expanding the application to process incoming video data more effectively.  I'm focusing on parsing the video stream within the media element and utilizing the image and audio stream together.  I'm also building out logic to properly utilize the video elements for future image capture and analysis. This should significantly improve how video is managed.
